subject: Regional deployment guardrails and VPC hosting statement

Subject: Regional deployment guardrails and quick statement (initial)

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clarity on Solstice's regulatory needs. Per our discussion, I've pulled together a short summary of the hosting guardrails we can commit to for EU-bound workloads. This is intended to be a concise operational statement you can share with your security/compliance team while we produce the formal, signed pack.

Key points (high level):
- Primary data processing and persistent storage can be constrained to eu-west-1 (Ireland) or another EU region you specify.
- We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations; key material can remain under your KMS/HSM tenancy.
- Private control plane option: we can deploy the control plane with a private endpoint in your VPC (customer-managed) or provide a private link with strict egress controls.
- Audit and application logs: we can deliver encrypted audit logs to a customer-owned bucket in your EU project/account.
- Egress controls: default posture is deny-all outbound with allow-lists for Redwood endpoints you explicitly approve.

I've attached a short PDF that summarizes the above and a checklist for the next steps (runbook + required approvals). If this aligns, I'll coordinate with Marissa and Rishi to produce a signed statement and the CAIQ/SIG artifacts you requested.

Attachment: redwood-region-commitment-20260503.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the target EU region (we default to eu-west-1).
2) Confirm whether you'd prefer the control plane inside your account (we'll provide IaC templates) or Redwood-managed private-link.
3) Specify any third-party egress destinations to be whitelisted.

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through any of the bullets.

Thanks,
Jonas

Thanks Jonas — that helps. A few clarifying questions from our InfoSec team before we escalate to procurement: 

1) Can you confirm in writing that Solstice customer data at rest (including logs and backups) will not leave the EU unless we explicitly approve a cross-border transfer? We need a commitment that replicas/archives remain region-restricted by default.

2) For KMS/BYOK: will Redwood support a model where key operations (encrypt/decrypt) require a customer-held key that Redwood cannot export? Put differently, will you support a KMS path that ensures Redwood only ever sees encrypted data at rest without having the key material?

3) Control plane in customer account: is it a supported deployment model today and do you provide the terraform modules/runbooks? If not, what's the timeline?

4) Can you provide the SIG/CAIQ answers and a redacted SOC 2 report? Our vendor onboarding requires those artifacts before we can approve production flow.

Also include a network diagram that shows how VPC peering/private link and audit log delivery would look. 

If you can respond by EOD Thursday that would be great — procurement is waiting on our side.

Best,

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Below is the formal operational statement and the artifacts we've attached/shared. This message is intended to be a short, consumable confirmation you can include in your vendor package; the attached PDF is the official statement we can sign if that meets your procurement needs.

Redwood Inference — Regional deployment guardrails (Solstice Health, EU)

1) Data residency and backups
- Default behavior: Persistent customer data (customer objects, model inputs/outputs persisted to storage, audit logs, and backups) is stored in the EU region you specify (default: eu-west-1).
- Replication policy: Cross-region replication is disabled by default. Any replication out of the specified EU region requires an explicit written change request and approval from Solstice.

2) Key management (BYOK)
- We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs.
- Key material: Customers retain ownership of key material. When configured for BYOK the key never leaves the customer KMS/HSM; Redwood possesses only wrapped key references and performs crypto operations via KMS APIs under the customer's project/account permissions.
- Operational controls: Key usage is logged to the customer audit stream; Redwood does not export unwrapped key material.

3) Private control plane deployment models
- Customer-hosted control plane: We provide IaC templates and a runbook (attached) to deploy a lightweight control plane into a customer VPC. This is a supported option today for enterprise customers and has been used in recent private deployments.
- Redwood-managed private-link: Alternative option where the control plane is hosted by Redwood but accessible only through a private endpoint in your VPC. This option enforces network egress restrictions and minimizes inbound surface area.

4) Network, egress, and logging
- Network posture: Default deny-all egress; outbound allowed only to explicitly approved Redwood endpoints. We support customer-managed firewall rules and security groups.
- Audit logs: Encrypted audit logs (read-only) can be delivered to a customer-owned storage bucket in the agreed EU region. Splunk/Datadog forwarders or S3/GCS delivery supported.
- Peering/topology: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and Transit Gateway architectures; diagram attached in the runbook.

5) Artifacts and evidence
- SIG/CAIQ: We have completed SIG/CAIQ answers and have made a copy available in the shared drive (link below).
- SOC 2: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Mina has the redacted file ready; I will coordinate a secure transfer.

Attachments and links provided:
- redwood-geo-deployment-statement-20260506.pdf (formal statement; 3 pages)
- private-deploy-runbook-draft.docx (IaC snippets and network diagram)
- Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xq_example_runbook (SIG/CAIQ bundle and SOC 2 transfer instructions)
- DocuSign path (if you need an executed statement): https://app.docusign.com/rooms/ABC-123-Solstice-Geo-Statement

If this meets Solstice's needs I can have Marissa/Legal sign the PDF and we can return the executed copy via DocuSign. If you need any additional controls (e.g., dedicated egress appliances, private HSM hosting, or contractual addenda around data flow approvals) let me know and we'll scope them.
